issues.legal_issue: A tenant’s wilful default in paying rent is not established where the landlord withdrew rent deposited by the tenant before filing for eviction, the eviction pleadings identify no unpaid period, and the alleged default rests on an unproved higher rent.
material_facts: The tenants applied to deposit rent in court after the landlord did not respond to their requests for bank details, and the landlord withdrew the rent deposited for the relevant months before filing the eviction petitions.
The applications for permission to deposit rent were dismissed, but the landlord had received the deposited rent before seeking eviction.
The appellate authority found that the tenants’ stated rents were correct and that the landlord had not proved the higher rents he claimed.
The eviction petitions did not identify any month or period for which rent had not been paid; the alleged default was based on failure to pay the higher rent claimed by the landlord.
The landlord had not issued the notice contemplated by the statutory explanation to the wilful-default provision.
issues.conclusion: The tenants did not commit wilful default, and the High Court was right to set aside eviction on that ground.
issues.legal_principle: Under Section 10(2)(i) of the Tamil Nadu Buildings (Lease & Rent Control) Act, 1960, read with its proviso and Explanation, eviction for rent default requires a wilful default; the Explanation treats default as wilful if it continues after the landlord issues the specified two-month notice claiming rent. Whether default is wilful is a mixed question of law and fact. Under Section 25, the High Court may reverse appellate findings that are illegal, erroneous or perverse. Rent deposited in court after the landlord refused to receive it is not, by itself, a valid payment or tender where the deposit application is rejected; however, a landlord who withdraws the deposited rent before filing for eviction cannot claim default for that period. The Court also relied on Dakaya @ Dakaiah v. Anjani, (1995) 6 SCC 500.

rule.if: rent_control_eviction_case and landlord_withdrew_deposited_rent_before_filing and pleadings_identified_no_unpaid_period and landlord_failed_to_prove_higher_rent and no_prior_demand_notice

predicates.rent_control_eviction_case: A landlord brought a rent-control proceeding seeking a tenant’s eviction for alleged non-payment of rent.
predicates.landlord_withdrew_deposited_rent_before_: The landlord withdrew rent deposited by the tenant before the landlord filed the eviction proceeding.
predicates.pleadings_identified_no_unpaid_period: The eviction pleadings did not identify a particular month or period for which rent remained unpaid.
predicates.landlord_failed_to_prove_higher_rent: The landlord did not prove that the rent due was higher than the amount the tenant said was agreed.
predicates.no_prior_demand_notice: The landlord did not issue the notice claiming rent that would make continued default wilful under the applicable rule.

issues.definition: When a rent-control eviction proceeding for non-payment has these facts, wilful default is not established.

issues.legal_issue: A tenant’s assertion that a landlord is only a co-owner does not establish denial of the landlord’s title when the tenant lacks notice of the landlord’s derivative title and does not renounce the tenancy or claim an adverse title.
material_facts: The tenants became tenants before the landlord acquired title under a release deed from the former owner.
The landlord did not notify the tenants of the transfer, and no new lease deeds were executed in the landlord’s favour.
After the former owner died, the tenants paid rent to the landlord.

In response to an eviction notice, the tenants said that the landlord was not the absolute owner because the former owner had left other heirs; they also said they did not know about the release deed.

The tenants continued to acknowledge the landlord-tenant relationship, continued paying rent, did not claim title for themselves or another person, and did not persist in the co-ownership assertion after learning of the release deed.
issues.conclusion: The tenants had not denied the landlord’s title in the sense required for eviction, and the landlord failed to establish that ground.
issues.legal_principle: Section 10(2)(vii) of the Tamil Nadu Buildings (Lease & Rent Control) Act, 1960 requires both a denial of the landlord’s title or a claim of permanent tenancy and that the denial or claim be not bona fide. A tenant denies title by renouncing the status of tenant and setting up a title or right inconsistent with the tenancy, in the tenant or a third person. Where the landlord’s title is derivative, an assertion that the landlord is a co-owner, made without notice of the transfer and without renouncing the tenancy, does not amount to denial of title. The principle against approbating and reprobating is reflected in Section 116 of the Evidence Act and Section 111(g) of the Transfer of Property Act.

rule.if: rent_control_eviction_case and landlord_claimed_derivative_title and tenant_lacked_notice_of_transfer and tenant_asserted_coownership and tenant_continued_acknowledging_tenancy and tenant_claimed_no_adverse_title

predicates.rent_control_eviction_case: A landlord brought a rent-control proceeding seeking a tenant’s eviction on the ground that the tenant denied the landlord’s title.
predicates.landlord_claimed_derivative_title: The landlord’s asserted ownership came through a transfer from a person who had previously let the property to the tenant.
predicates.tenant_lacked_notice_of_transfer: The tenant had not been informed of the transfer by which the landlord acquired title.
predicates.tenant_asserted_coownership: The tenant said that the landlord was only a co-owner because other heirs of the former owner also had interests in the property.
predicates.tenant_continued_acknowledging_tenancy: The tenant continued to treat the relationship with the landlord as a tenancy and continued paying rent to the landlord.
predicates.tenant_claimed_no_adverse_title: The tenant did not claim ownership for themself or another person and did not maintain an adverse title claim.

issues.definition: When a tenant in a rent-control eviction proceeding makes a co-ownership assertion in the stated circumstances while continuing to acknowledge the tenancy and claiming no adverse title, denial of the landlord’s title is not established.
